attribution: Jardelsliumba — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Vale do Pati, Chapada Diamantina National Park, Bahia
alt: Wide view over the Pati valley with its sandstone ridges and green slopes in the Chapada Diamantina
caption: The Vale do Pati, a roadless sandstone valley inside the Chapada Diamantina National Park that is crossed on foot over four to five days; families in the valley host walkers overnight.

attribution: Mikaelli Ernesto — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Vale do Pati, Chapada Diamantina National Park, Bahia
alt: Landscape photograph of the Pati valley with plateau walls and vegetation
caption: The Pati trail runs along steep sandstone walls and across plateau and valley floor; this is the terrain of the multi-day crossing, which is muddier but has fuller waterfalls in the rainy months.

commonsFile: File:Sunset near Morro do Pai Inácio, Palmeiras, Bahia.jpg
attribution: Rosino — CC BY-SA 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Morro do Pai Inácio, Palmeiras, Bahia
alt: Sunset sky over the flat-topped Morro do Pai Inácio and the surrounding plateau landscape
caption: Morro do Pai Inácio, the flat-topped sandstone hill beside the BR-242 near Lençóis, is the classic sunset viewpoint and a short, easy first walk before the longer trek.

attribution: Adelano Lázaro Ferreira — Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Cachoeira da Fumaça, Chapada Diamantina, Bahia
alt: Tall waterfall dropping from the edge of a plateau into a deep valley
caption: The Cachoeira da Fumaça, one of the tallest waterfalls in Brazil, drops from the plateau edge near Vale do Capão; it is a rainy-season highlight when the flow is strongest and an optional extra on the Pati side.

attribution: MAURICIO GOMES DE OLIVEIRA — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Clear blue water in a cave pool lit by a shaft of daylight
caption: Poço Azul, a cave lake with very clear blue water that visitors can float in; it belongs to the group of cave sites reached on a day trip from Lençóis.

commonsFile: File:Gruta da Lapa Doce na Chapada Diamantina.jpg
attribution: Heris Luiz Cordeiro Rocha — CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
location: Gruta da Lapa Doce, Iraquara, Bahia
alt: Large limestone cave chamber with stalagmites and stalactites inside the Lapa Doce cave
caption: Gruta da Lapa Doce near Iraquara, a walk-through limestone cave with large chambers and formations; one of the cave stops of the rest-and-explore day on the western edge of the Chapada.

attribution: Paul R. Burley — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Colourful colonial buildings and cobbled square at the Pelourinho in Salvador
caption: The Pelourinho in the historic centre of Salvador, a UNESCO-listed ensemble of colonial houses and churches where Afro-Brazilian music, food and religion are part of everyday life; the trip starts and ends here.

attribution: Paul R. Burley — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: The Lacerda Elevator tower connecting the upper and lower towns of Salvador
caption: The Lacerda Elevator links Salvador's upper town to the lower town and the old port market area; it is the quick, cheap way to move between the Pelourinho and the waterfront.

attribution: Julia Rubinic — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Capoeira players in a circle in a street in Salvador
caption: Capoeira, the Afro-Brazilian martial art and dance, is practised in Salvador's streets and academies; the group can watch a roda or take a beginners' class with a local mestre.

commonsFile: File:Samba Junino no Recôncavo - Independência da Bahia em Cachoeira 24.jpg
attribution: SouDiana — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Members of a local samba group performing in the street in Cachoeira during a festival
caption: A local samba group performing in Cachoeira, the river town in the Recôncavo where Afro-Bahian traditions, candomblé houses and the Boa Morte sisterhood are strongest; photographed during a festival, not in February.

attribution: Portoquá — CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Women washing clothes in the Lençóis river beside the town
caption: The Lençóis river runs through the old diamond-mining town of Lençóis, the base for the first and last nights in the Chapada; the town's riverbank is a place for an evening walk.

attribution: Dimitry B. — CC BY 2.0, via Wikimedia Commons
alt: Sunset over the hills and rooftops around Lençóis
caption: Evening light over Lençóis, a 19th-century diamond town at the foot of the Chapada Diamantina plateau, where guesthouses and trek agencies make it the natural base for the valley crossing.
